module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1064

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1064](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1064)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Nat Filter Topology

namespace Erdos1064

/--
Let $ϕ(n)$ be the Euler's totient function, then the $n$ satisfies $ϕ(n)>ϕ(n - ϕ(n))$
have asymptotic density 1.
Reference: [LuPo02] Luca, Florian and Pomerance, Carl, On some problems of {M}\polhk akowski-{S}chinzel and {E}rd\H
os concerning the arithmetical functions {$\phi$} and
{$\sigma$}. Colloq. Math.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1064 : {n | φ n > φ (n - φ n)}.HasDensity 1 := by
  sorry

/--
Let $ϕ(n)$ be the Euler's totient function, there exist infinitely many $n$
such that $ϕ(n)< ϕ(n - ϕ(n))$
Reference: [GLW01] Grytczuk, A. and Luca, F. and W\'ojtowicz, M., A conjecture of {E}rdős concerning inequalities for the
{E}uler totient function.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1064.variants.k2 : {n | φ n < φ (n - φ n)}.Infinite := by
  apply Set.infinite_of_injective_forall_mem (f := fun k : ℕ => 30 * 2 ^ k)
  · intro a b hab
    simp only at hab
    have : (2 : ℕ) ^ a = 2 ^ b := by omega
    exact Nat.pow_right_injective (le_refl 2) this
  · intro k
    simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
    have hφ : Nat.totient (30 * 2 ^ k) = 8 * 2 ^ k := by
      have h : 30 * 2 ^ k = 2 ^ (k + 1) * 15 := by ring
      rw [h, Nat.totient_mul (by norm_num),
        Nat.totient_prime_pow Nat.prime_two (by omega),
        show Nat.totient 15 = 8 from rfl, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
      ring
    have hsub : 30 * 2 ^ k - Nat.totient (30 * 2 ^ k) = 22 * 2 ^ k := by
      rw [hφ]
      omega
    have hφsub : Nat.totient (22 * 2 ^ k) = 10 * 2 ^ k := by
      rw [show 22 * 2 ^ k = 2 ^ (k + 1) * 11 by ring,
        Nat.totient_mul (by norm_num), Nat.totient_prime_pow (by norm_num) (by omega),
        show Nat.totient 11 = 10 from rfl, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
      ring
    rw [hsub, hφ, hφsub]
    have : (0 : ℕ) < 2 ^ k := pow_pos (by norm_num) k
    omega

open Asymptotics Filter

/--
For any function $f(n)=o(n)$,
we have $\phi(n)>\phi(n-\phi(n))+f(n)$ for almost all $n$.
Reference:
[LuPo02] Luca, Florian and Pomerance, Carl, On some problems of {M}\polhk akowski-{S}chinzel and {E}rd\H
os concerning the arithmetical functions {$\phi$} and
{$\sigma$}. Colloq. Math. (2002), 111--130.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1064.variants.general_function (f : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hf : (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ))) :
    {n : ℕ | φ (n - φ n) + f n < φ n}.HasDensity 1 := by
  sorry


end Erdos1064

reformulations.difference: The source is the erdosproblems.com remark taken from Luca–Pomerance: "for any function f(n) = o(n), we have φ(n) > φ(n − φ(n)) + f(n) for almost all n". There f can be real-valued and possibly negative. Luca–Pomerance, Theorem 3(i), phrase it with a positive ε(x) → 0: the inequality φ(n − φ(n)) < φ(n) − nε(n) fails for n > 1 only on a set of density 0. The Lean quantifies only over f : ℕ → ℕ with (f n : ℝ) =o[atTop] (n : ℝ). It states that {n : ℕ | φ (n - φ n) + f n < φ n} has natural density 1 (`Set.HasDensity`, i.e. |S ∩ [0,b)|/b → 1).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: ℕ-valued f is a special case of real-valued f, so the source's version implies the Lean one. For the converse, take real f = o(n) and put g n = ⌈max (f n) 0⌉₊. Then 0 ≤ g n ≤ |f n| + 1, so g = o(n). Since f n ≤ g n, the inequality φ(n−φ n) + g n < φ n implies φ(n−φ n) + f n < φ n. So the set for f contains the set for g, and a superset of a density-1 set has density 1. I proved this ↔ in Lean (`general_function_nat_iff_real`, compiled against the module, standard axioms only). The ε-form of Luca–Pomerance Theorem 3(i) is also equivalent. Given f, take ε(x) = (f(⌊x⌋)+1)/x for x ≥ 1 (and 1 below that). It is positive, tends to 0, and nε(n) > f(n). Given ε, take f(n) = ⌈nε(n)⌉, which is o(n). Truncated subtraction never fires, since φ n ≤ n. Mathlib's φ 0 = 0 matters only at n ∈ {0,1}, which does not affect density. With f = 0 the variant is literally `erdos_1064`; I checked this in Lean.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/1064 (direct access is blocked by Cloudflare; I read the rendered page through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/1064). Statement: 'Prove that φ(n) > φ(n − φ(n)) for almost all n, but that φ(n) < φ(n − φ(n)) for infinitely many n'. Status PROVED. The remarks include GLW01, LuPo02 and the f(n)=o(n) strengthening.

https://math.dartmouth.edu/~carlp/PDF/paper127.pdf — F. Luca, C. Pomerance, On some problems of Mąkowski–Schinzel and Erdős concerning the arithmetical functions φ and σ, Colloq. Math. 92 (2002), 111–130. Introduction (conjecture (6)/(7)) and Theorem 3(i)–(ii).

https://publi.math.unideb.hu/contents/2001 and https://publi.math.unideb.hu/paper/718/download/10_5486_PMD_2001_2340.pdf — A. Grytczuk, F. Luca, M. Wójtowicz, A conjecture of Erdős concerning inequalities for the Euler totient function, Publ. Math. Debrecen 59 (2001), 9–16. Quotes Guy B42; conjecture (EC1) ρ(A)=1 and (EC2) C infinite; density defined as #{m∈M : m<n}/n.
review.notes:
I checked every declaration and found no misformalization.

- `erdos_1064`: `{n | φ n > φ (n - φ n)}.HasDensity 1` states the first half of the problem ('for almost all n'). This is the source's claim and GLW01's (EC1). The density convention (counting m < b over ℕ) is the same as GLW01's. The value n = 0 is never in the set, and the n = 1 junk case (φ 0 = 0) cannot affect density.
- `erdos_1064.variants.k2`: `{n | φ n < φ (n - φ n)}.Infinite` is the second half of the problem (GLW01's (EC2)). It is fully proved in the file with the family n = 30·2^k (= 15·2^(k+1), the source's own example). `#print axioms` shows only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
- Sanity checks by `#eval`: in Lean, A_< begins 30, 60, 66, 120, as erdosproblems.com says. The equality set contains 3·2^k.
- `erdos_1064.variants.general_function`: equivalent to the source remark and to Luca–Pomerance Theorem 3(i); see the reformulation entry.
- Status: all three are tagged `research solved`, which matches the source (PROVED: part 2 by GLW01, part 1 and the o(n) strengthening by LuPo02). There are no answer slots or formal_proof records.

Structure only, not the mathematics: the source's problem is one conjunction. The file states the first half under the main name and the second half under the unusual name `variants.k2`; other files use `parts.ii`. Together the two declarations cover the full problem, and each docstring matches its own Lean statement.

I did not read the original Erdős source [Er80f] or Guy's UPINT B42 directly. The statement is corroborated by erdosproblems.com, by GLW01 (which quotes B42) and by LuPo02.
